items.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewer mentions Toru Takemitsu's praise for George Russell's book and notes that Takemitsu translated the book into Japanese. George Russell does not provide any personal anecdote, statement of meeting, or description of a direct professional or social relationship with Takemitsu in the pro

ctx.x: I must have been working on a book. That’s all I’ve been working on for 30 years. I mean, it’s not all I’ve been working on. I’ve been doing the commissions and stuff, but it’s the main thing.

If anyone has picked up on this oral history right at this point, let me say that the book we’re talking about is The Lydian Chromatic Concept of Tonal Organization, volume I: The Art and Science of Tonal Gravity. I want to read to you something that I found very interesting that Toru Takemitsu – I hope I’m pronouncing his name corrrectly – said. He said, “The Lydian Chromatic Concept is one of the two most splendid books about music.” I’m going to jump down here. “Though I’m considered a contemporary music…
Blessings to – my man. What’s his name?
